headline: High-risk default workspace sharing and tool-enabled coding agent create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure when paired with a non-runnable reference list.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a non-runnable curated collection with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot ingest Agent B directly. Agent B can read workspace files, use MCP, and browse, and its shared filesystem model means any content placed in the workspace can be treated as input. The pair therefore has a plausible injection path through files, though not a direct default bridge.
conditions: IF Agent B reads attacker-controlled workspace files as instructions
IF a file from Agent A's repository is copied into Agent B's workspace
mitigations: Keep Agent B in a separate workspace from any untrusted content
Disable MCP servers not explicitly needed
Require manual review of file-derived instructions before tool use
Use read-only mounts for reference material
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for workspace inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches no data classes and has no egress, but Agent B reads and writes workspace files and has broad network egress plus browser use. If sensitive files are present in the shared workspace, B can transmit them externally. A does not add leakage risk, but B alone makes the pair unsafe for sensitive workspace data.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in Agent B's workspace
IF Agent B is configured to send file contents to its model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Do not place secrets in the shared workspace
Restrict Agent B network egress to approved endpoints
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for B
Rotate any secrets already stored in workspace files
requires-engineering: enforce content filtering before uploads

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has no write or execution capabilities, so it cannot conflict operationally. Agent B can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses in a workspace-shared concurrency model. Because the pair shares state via filesystem, concurrent instances of B can corrupt or overwrite each other; A does not mitigate this. The conflict is driven entirely by B's default workspace semantics.
conditions: IF two Agent B instances operate in the same VS Code workspace
IF Agent B modifies git state or workspace files without external locking
mitigations: Run only one Agent B instance per workspace
Use separate git branches per task
Pause auto-commit or auto-edit workflows
Add a manual lock file before edits
requires-engineering: implement workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B can act on outputs from tools and browser content, while Agent A provides no verification or authoritative facts because it is only a reference collection. The main cascade risk is that B may treat copied material or generated snippets as trusted and then write files or modify git state. A does not create the cascade, but B can amplify unverified inputs into actions.
conditions: IF Agent B uses copied text from Agent A's repository as authoritative
IF Agent B commits or edits files based on unverified browser or MCP output
mitigations: Require a human review before commits
Verify facts against a second source before action
Disable auto-apply for generated patches
Keep reference collections separate from action workspaces
requires-engineering: add verification gates before write actions

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for Agent A, and Agent B only exposes generic workspace code and browser screenshots. The pair therefore has no proven compliance breach pathway from the profiles alone. Because the evidence is sparse and both are docs-only, uncertainty remains but does not justify escalation.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Agent B's workspace
IF a deployment policy requires residency or retention guarantees not shown here
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the workspace
Review vendor residency and retention terms before use
Limit screenshots to non-sensitive content
Document data-handling policy for the workspace
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets
